summary: Verified from the GSC API (service account, siteOwner), site_signal, web_vitals, site_improvement_ledger, git log and live curls. Probe outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RyanRealty/9fe9d814-a247-5921-8288-dab9436e06db/scratchpad/gsc-trend/probe*.txt; long-form notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RyanRealty/9fe9d814-a247-5921-8288-dab9436e06db/scratchpad/gsc-trend/notes.md. WHAT IS SLIPPING: overall organic clicks are not falling. The last 4 weeks (2026-08-24..09-20) had 523 clicks, the best 4-week block on record (June peak block was 480). Impressions are falling: 2,239/day on 09-07, 996/day on 09-20. Week 09-14..09-20 had 9,539 impressions vs 12,489 the week before (-24%) while clicks rose (138 vs 115). Average position 'improved' to 11.4 only because low-ranked impressions dropped out. The drop has three parts: (1) the intended de-indexing of S. Oregon and sentinel listing pages (SITE-27/SITE-33, 09-08/09); (2) Central Oregon listing-detail impressions falling (4,296 to 2,544) while listing URLs keep changing (1,234 of 7,329 listing keys, 16.8%, seen under more than one URL; variants return 200 plus a moving canonical, not a 301); (3) community, city and central-oregon classes falling, with /cities and /homes-for-sale/{city} dropping faster (-45% and -68%) than the site (-29%) in the 3 days after the 09-17 title/H1 collision. The real ranking slip is on the money pages. Community pages lost 3 to 14 positions on their own names since early July (/communities/brasada-ranch p21.6 to p35.8, /communities/tetherow p40.2 to p47.1, /communities/black-butte-ranch p33.9 to p38.5). City and 'homes for sale' target queries never ranked (p26 to p42), and all 23 target queries had 0 clicks. /homes-for-sale/bend had 0 impressions 09-06..09-21. The homepage ranks p45 for 'ryan realty'. The only sustained click drop (07-27..08-23: 337 vs 480, -30%, position 13.9 to 17.5) coincides with the late-July sitemap/deploy outage (124348def 'every deploy was ERROR', aa56d308d 'sitemap P0 fix never worked', 0dbf2f1cc '18% of paginated rows silently dropped') and with Wave D + zero-inventory noindex (07-22/23). WHY THE LOOP DOES NOT REACT: its GSC benchmark is 100% a rank tracker's quoted queries (153 of 153 rows, 0 clicks), yet the scoreboard says 'gsc: ok' and the brief says 'Ranking is not the served class'. Its GSC store keeps top-25 pages or queries per day, about 5% of impressions. Its Learn step writes actual_delta=0 because it matches '/blog/x' against stored full URLs (8 of 12 learned rows are false zeros, including a real CTR loss on the Sunriver title rewrite). Only 1 ledger row was written in September, while the site queue minted SITE-01 through SITE-180 and landed 474 commits in 14 days. GA4 has attributed at most 5 google/organic sessions per week since 07-13 (GSC: 71 to 151 clicks per week). The MP page_view mirror (416911b31, 08-10) floods '(not set)' sessions. Browser events were dead 08-19..08-31 as well as since 09-18. RUM has been swamped since 09-13 by 404 renders of dead /_next/image URLs (0 to 25,511 rows/day). Even mobile-only, place classes are 'poor' LCP (city 5,068 ms, neighborhood 9,924 ms, subdivision 4,624 ms p75). Correlations with commits are leads, not verdicts.

findings.title: The loop's ranking signal is a rank tracker plus a 5% sample, so it reports 'gsc: ok' while money pages slip
findings.claim: Every GSC number the loop reads is either synthetic or truncated. target_query_benchmark matches only a rank tracker's quoted queries (0 clicks). site_signal keeps top-25 pages/queries per day. The scoreboard marks gsc 'ok' from a row count. As a result the brief says 'Ranking is not the served class' and no ranking work is seeded, while community pages lose 3 to 14 positions and site impressions fall 24% week over week.
findings.evidence: probe13: 153/153 benchmark rows (last 28d) are quoted/bracketed-only, 0 plain, 0 clicks. probe10: quoted queries appear ~3 impr/day for 85-111 consecutive days. Migration 20260610230500 line 37 strips quotes and uses ilike '%q%'. lib/data/loop/signals.ts 463-467 status 'ok' unless error. loop-brief.txt 31-32. app/api/cron/marketing-snapshot-gsc/route.ts lines 62 and 99 (top 25). probe3 vs probe8: 2,721 of ~55,187 impressions visible (4.9%). scripts/seed-gsc-ranking-queue.ts (8a2c71e, 09-22) reads the full API but is dry-run, one window, no trend.
findings.why_it_matters: Matt's mission is being seen. The loop is the only thing that turns measurement into work, and it cannot see the slip it is supposed to fix. Every 'Run the loop' serves UX nodes because ranking reads healthy.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Add a full-fidelity GSC store: nightly API pulls of page x date and query x page x date (rowLimit 25000, paginate) for a trailing 16 months into dedicated tables (e.g. gsc_page_daily, gsc_query_page_daily), with a page_class column from one shared route classifier. (2) Rebuild target_query_benchmark on that store, match the query exactly (lowercased), and EXCLUDE quoted, bracketed and operator queries (keep them in a separate tracker view if wanted). (3) Scoreboard gsc status = per-class 28d clicks/impressions/impression-weighted position vs the prior 28d and vs 90d, Central Oregon only, and 'degraded' when a money class (community, city, homes-for-sale city/type, subdivision, home) loses 15% or more of impressions or 3 or more positions. (4) loop-brief seeds a ranking node from any degraded class automatically; make seed-gsc-ranking-queue.ts consume the stored trend instead of a one-window pull.

findings.title: Learn writes actual_delta=0 whenever a GSC window cannot be read (path vs full URL), closing SEO experiments as if measured
findings.claim: scripts/loop-learn-close-windows.ts matches ledger surfaces like '/blog/x' against site_signal surfaces stored as 'https://ryan-realty.com/blog/x'. It gets 0 rows and then writes actual_delta = 0 with verdict 'inconclusive'. Openness is actual_delta IS NULL, so the window counts as learned. 8 of the 12 'measured' rows are false zeros. At least one hid a real loss (Sunriver title rewrite).
findings.evidence: probe19: 0 rows by path vs 28 rows by full URL, window 2026-06-10..07-08. loop-learn-close-windows.ts line 66 (.in('surface', surfaces)), line 186 (actualDelta = 0), pageSeries has no source filter. signals.ts line 422 counts open only when actual_delta == null. probe7: 5 seo_title_rewrite + jsonld + content_new_market_report + legacy_redirect rows = 0/inconclusive. Sunriver baseline CTR 3.4% -> 1.51% (20c/1,327i, 07-13..08-09, probe11) -> 0.75% (7c/937i, 08-23..09-19, probe8), at a steady ~p6.8.
findings.why_it_matters: THE LOOP's Learn step is how the shop learns which title/content/canonical changes move rankings. It has been learning 'nothing happened' from a join bug, so the same failed tactics can be repeated.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalize surfaces on both sides (strip origin and trailing slash, or store path for scope=page). Filter pageSeries by source='gsc_search_analytics_api'. On no data, leave actual_delta NULL and set verdict 'unmeasurable' with a gap note, so the window stays visible. Add a unit test with a full-URL fixture. Re-run Learn for the 8 June seo-aeo rows against the full store (or the API) and record the real deltas.

findings.title: Ranking-affecting ships (titles, canonicals, redirects, index policy, sitemaps, ISR) land with no ledger row and no GSC readback
findings.claim: In September the site queue minted SITE-01 through SITE-180 and landed 474 commits in 14 days, many of which change what Google sees. The ledger got 1 row. SITE nodes that are 'blocked on measurement' plan to read GA4 (dead) and page-level Search Console (not stored). So no SEO-affecting change is tied to its effect, and inflections cannot be attributed except by hand, as in this audit.
findings.evidence: probe7: 20 ledger rows, 1 with shipped_at in 2026-09. loop-brief.txt line 92: 406 of 474 commits in 14 days have no node and no ledger row; site commits with a Node trailer 275/293. SEO-affecting commits with no ledger row include 469a58106 (09-09 one canonical per listing), 11cfbe523 (09-09 out-of-area leave index/sitemap), ec52e2026 (09-08), 446d95677 (09-08 title budget/noindex follow), 9794e028d (09-13 images unoptimized), ffcc52e80 (09-17 H1s), 136088a (09-22 blog 301). loop-brief lines 42-56: SITE-01/04/05/08/23/32 re-open 2026-10-05..11-08 on GA4 or GSC clicks.
findings.why_it_matters: Matt asked why the loop is not reaching its goals. It cannot close the measure-learn half of THE LOOP for the one goal that matters (being seen), so it keeps building without knowing if the last build helped or hurt.
findings.proposed_fix: Make a ledger row mandatory (a gate in npm run push / ci:process-canon) for any commit touching metadata, canonical, robots, sitemap, redirects, middleware routing, ISR/revalidate, or URL builders (lib/slug.ts). The row names the page class, a GSC metric from the full store (gsc-trend-1), the predicted direction and a 28-day window. The measurer closes it from that store.

findings.title: Community money pages lost 3 to 14 positions on their own names since early July, with signals split across many URLs
findings.claim: The slip Matt feels is concentrated on the resort-community pages, the targets of 11 of the 23 target queries. Each name's impressions are spread across the community page, subdivision plats, blog posts, housing-market pages, filtered /homes-for-sale URLs and dozens of listing variants. The decline started in the 07-13/07-20 weeks and deepened through the late-July sitemap outage.
findings.evidence: probe15: /communities/brasada-ranch p21.6 -> p35.8 (1,213i -> 671i), /communities/tetherow p40.2 -> p47.1, /communities/black-butte-ranch p33.9 -> p38.5, /communities/broken-top p21.0 -> p23.7. Query 'black butte ranch' hits 11 pages late (incl. /homes-for-sale/black-butte-ranch?propertySubTypes=Condominium p54.8, /housing-market/black-butte-ranch p86.5); 'brasada ranch' hits 65 pages. probe8 community class position 23.2 (07-06) -> 35.0 (08-24) -> 20.0 (09-14); impressions 1,864 (08-24) -> 383 (09-14, 6d). probe11 /communities/brasada-ranch weekly impressions 472 (07-06) -> 21 (07-27). Nearby commits: 96f76ca14 (07-22), bff8c6077 (07-23), 250044022 (07-28 geography redirects retarget to community pages).
findings.why_it_matters: These are the pages Matt built the site to win ('search by subdivisions ... so much information to expose'). Positions 20 to 48 get almost no clicks. All community target queries had 0 clicks in both windows.
findings.proposed_fix: Run a ranking node per community from the full GSC store: pull query x page for the community's name set and pick the one page that should rank. Consolidate or de-target cannibals: point filtered /homes-for-sale?propertySubTypes= and /housing-market/{community} titles away from the bare name, and make subdivision plats link up to the community with a subordinate title. Check the 07-22/07-23 changes (Wave D search matrix, zero-inventory noindex) for community-page link loss or noindex. Record a ledger row per change (gsc-trend-3).

findings.title: City and 'homes for sale' target pages have never ranked; /homes-for-sale/bend has zero impressions
findings.claim: The p1 city-buy and agent queries ('homes for sale bend oregon', 'bend or homes for sale', 'bend oregon realtor', 'redmond/sisters oregon homes for sale') rank p26 to p42 or not at all. The declared target URL /homes-for-sale/bend gets no impressions. /cities/bend ranks p62 for 'bend oregon realtor'. Since 09-17 the /cities and /homes-for-sale/{city} impressions are falling faster than the site.
findings.evidence: probe8 unquoted then/now: bend oregon realtor p19.2 -> p37.1; sisters oregon homes for sale p27.9 -> p42.4; redmond oregon homes for sale p30.5 -> p35.5; homes for sale bend oregon 5i p26.0 -> 3i p38.7. probe15: /homes-for-sale/bend 0 queries 0 impressions 09-06..09-21; /cities/bend 70i/0c 09-06..09-16; /cities/{slug} -45% and /homes-for-sale/{city} -68% vs site -29% (09-14..16 vs 09-18..20) after ffcc52e80. probe4 target_queries: the 6 p1 city-buy queries target /homes-for-sale/bend (x2), /homes-for-sale/bend/luxury, /homes-for-sale/redmond, /homes-for-sale/sisters and /cities/bend.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the highest-volume buyer queries in the market. Ranking p26 to p60 means no organic buyer leads from the city layer, however much inventory the pages expose.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one indexable page per city for the 'homes for sale {city}' intent. Either make /homes-for-sale/{city} the canonical, indexable, server-rendered target (and verify why it has 0 impressions: canonical, noindex, rewrite or sitemap absence, per the seo-technical reader), or retarget target_queries to /cities/{city} and give /homes-for-sale/{city} a distinct title/H1 (the verified 09-17 collision). Add these queries to the full-store benchmark (gsc-trend-1) and track them weekly.

findings.title: Listing canonicals move with every geo reclassification; 16.8% of listing keys are indexed under more than one URL and variants 200 instead of 301
findings.claim: The listing canonical embeds city/neighborhood/subdivision. When the boundary classifier or URL builder changes (SITE-22, SITE-23 Brasada sentinel, SITE-27/33), the canonical moves. Old URLs still return 200 with a rel=canonical, not a 301, so Google indexes several URLs per home and keeps re-learning them. Central Oregon listing-detail impressions fell 4,296 -> 2,544 in week 09-14 while clicks held.
findings.evidence: probe16: now (08-23..09-19) 1,234 of 7,329 listing keys under >1 URL (16.8%, 11,694 of 31,942 detail impressions, 132 of 376 detail clicks; 690 with an /outside-boundaries/ variant); June 262 of 3,983 (6.6%). probe20 live: outside-boundaries Brasada variant 200 -> canonical powell-butte path; Locksley URL Google shows (1,657i) now canonicalizes to /homes-for-sale/bend/mountain-view/providence/...; lazy-river-west now canonicalizes to a third path not in GSC. Builder: lib/slug.ts listingDetailPath (line 180), listingCanonicalHref (line 329); lib/data/listings/getListingCanonicalPathFields.ts; 469a58106 (09-09).
findings.why_it_matters: Listing detail is the largest click class (365 of 508 top-25 clicks in the last 4 weeks, probe3). Moving canonicals split signals and reset each listing's ranking history. Two variants also timed out at 40 s cold, which a crawler may count as a failed fetch.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the listing canonical stable per ListingKey (e.g. /homes-for-sale/{city}/{address-slug}-{key}, with city from the MLS City field only, never from polygon classification or subdivision). 308 every other path that ends in the same key to that canonical in middleware (resolve by key, no page render). Add a gate: the canonical for a fixed set of fixture listings must not change across a build unless an explicit migration list says so.

findings.title: No production monitor catches sitemap/deploy outages; the one sustained click loss came from one
findings.claim: The only multi-week click drop (-30%, 07-27..08-23) overlaps a stretch where deploys errored and the sitemaps were expiring, partial or dropping 18% of rows. It was found by successive agent passes, not by a monitor. Sitemaps kept breaking afterwards (09-09 geo.xml over the 300 s ceiling; 09-16 keyset paging).
findings.evidence: probe2: 07-27..08-23 337c vs 480c, position 13.9 -> 17.5. probe8/probe11: listing detail clicks 58 -> 36/30/31/34; subdivision position 16.4 -> 28.3 (08-17). Commits 124348def (07-30 'every deploy was ERROR'), aa56d308d (08-02 'sitemap P0 fix never worked'), 996ece96a (08-02 'the cause three passes have missed'), 0dbf2f1cc (08-03 '18% of paginated rows silently dropped'), 016671684 (09-09 geo.xml 300 s), a80e52e84 (09-16 keyset-paged listings sitemap), 1ac0f4ca7 (08-24 'drop Upstash from middleware so production can deploy').
findings.why_it_matters: Google's crawl of 8,000+ listing and place URLs depends on sitemaps. A silent sitemap regression costs weeks of rankings before anyone looks at GSC, and today nobody does (gsc-trend-1).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a daily cron that fetches the sitemap index and every child with a Googlebot UA. Assert 200 within a time budget and a URL count within +/-5% of the DAL's expected count per class. Write the result to site_signal (source=sitemap_probe) and page the loop/Matt digest on failure. Also pull the GSC Sitemaps API (submitted vs indexed) into the same table.

findings.title: GA4 has been blind to organic since mid-July; MP mirror floods (not set); browser stream also dead 08-19..08-31
findings.claim: GA4 attributes at most 5 organic sessions a week while GSC reports 71 to 151 clicks. The server-side MP page_view mirror (08-10) creates sessionless '(not set)' sessions that swamp the property. The browser gtag stream died on 08-19 after the 08-18 GTM/consent commits, came back partly on 09-01, and died again on 09-18. Every GA4-based accept test and ledger metric since mid-July is unusable.
findings.evidence: probe5/probe10: google/organic sessions 32, 23, 3, 4, -, -, 3, -, -, 5, -, 1 (weeks 06-29..09-14) vs GSC 111..138. Sessions 33 -> 4,237 (week 08-10), (not set) 4,211; probe14: (not set) 699/699 on 09-19. probe14: session_start/first_visit/user_engagement/scroll_depth/section_view/LCP absent 08-19..08-31, partial 09-01..09-17, absent from 09-19. Commits 416911b31 (08-10), 1224b1f31 + a732b9948 (08-18), 340fb066d (09-01), f1e2a90f9 (09-17). Mid-July cause UNVERIFIED (candidates 9a000a31b, 875049de3 on 07-10).
findings.why_it_matters: Conversion from organic cannot be measured, so 'seen then convert' has no funnel number. The site-queue nodes blocked on GA4 measurement (SITE-05/07/11/12) will read garbage on 2026-10-06.
findings.proposed_fix: Stop sending MP page_view to the main GA4 property, or send it with the visitor's _ga client_id and session_id so it stitches. Restore the browser tag (other reader's GTM fix). Add a daily guard in site_signal: GA4 google/organic sessions / GSC clicks must be >= 0.4, and browser session_start must be > 0, else alert and mark GA4-dependent ledger windows 'unmeasurable'. Re-baseline every GA4-based accept test after the fix.

findings.title: RUM is swamped by 404 renders of dead /_next/image URLs since 09-13; real mobile LCP on place pages is poor
findings.claim: Since images.unoptimized (09-13), requests for old /_next/image URLs render the full HTML 404 page, which mounts the web-vitals reporter. That is 20,000+ rows a day, 50 to 70% of all RUM, all desktop, flat by hour. Every p75 the loop reads is now a bot/404 number. Filtered to mobile, the ranking classes (city, neighborhood, place-type, subdivision, community, housing-market) are above the 4 s 'poor' LCP line.
findings.evidence: probe17: /_next/image rows 0/day 09-06..09-12, then 5,864, 25,511 (69.2%), 23,736, 22,431, 9,565, 1,533, 1,378, 1,510, 9,797 (09-21, 61.6%). 9794e028d 09-13 (next.config.ts line 139). probe9: 7d LCP p75 on /_next/image 9,876 ms, n=14,517; desktop 26,874 vs mobile 1,120. probe12 mobile p75: city 5,068, neighborhood 9,924, place-type 7,220, housing-market 5,240, subdivision 4,624, community 4,176, overall 3,492 (n=2,954). probe18: image-search impressions 191/day -> 128/day after 09-13.
findings.why_it_matters: Page experience is a ranking input and LCP is the loop's perf metric (ledger perf_lcp rows). Poisoned RUM hides real regressions and fakes others. Whatever is re-fetching dead image URLs at this rate is also spending crawl/render budget on 404s.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not mount WebVitalsReporter on not-found/error routes, and drop samples whose path starts with /_next/ in app/api/web-vitals/route.ts. Store UA class and navigator.webdriver, and exclude bots. 301 or serve legacy /_next/image?url= requests to the underlying image instead of a 404 page (keeps image search and cuts render cost). Pull CrUX (the field data Google uses) per origin and per top URL into site_signal as the loop's perf truth. Then work the mobile LCP of city/neighborhood/place-type pages.

findings.title: Headline impressions mix S. Oregon/sentinel inventory and a non-transactional query, so intended pruning reads as a slip
findings.claim: The 08-24..09-07 'peak' included 4,967/4,552/3,643 weekly impressions from S. Oregon city slugs plus outside-boundaries listing pages, and 1,652 impressions from 'apartments near northeast locksley drive bend or' (0 clicks). SITE-27/33 removed much of the out-of-area set on purpose. Site-wide totals therefore mix wanted and unwanted visibility.
findings.evidence: probe11 weekly detail impressions (S. Oregon + outside-boundaries): 1,336+3,631, 1,789+2,763, 2,393+1,250; week 09-14 (6d) 1,405+678. S. Oregon clicks 77 of 385 in 08-24..09-13. probe8/probe11 Locksley query 695/585/372 per week. Note: outside-boundaries also holds Central Oregon rural and Brasada Ranch homes (SITE-23), so it is not purely out-of-market.
findings.why_it_matters: Matt and the loop will chase the wrong number. The metric that tracks the mission is Central Oregon money-class visibility, not total impressions.
findings.proposed_fix: Report GSC by page class and by market (Central Oregon vs other) in the scoreboard and brief (part of gsc-trend-1). Exclude listings outside the service area from the headline. Fix the sentinel so Central Oregon rural homes do not share a bucket with out-of-area inventory.

findings.title: The homepage ranks ~p45 for the brand name 'ryan realty'
findings.claim: For 'ryan realty' the homepage sits at p45 in both July and September. Only the GBP-tagged URL ranks (p3). Homepage position across all queries swung p25 -> p41 -> p20 after the 08-10 and 09-07 title rewrites.
findings.evidence: probe15: / p45.1 (06-29..07-19, 8i) and p45.3 (08-31..09-20, 20i); /?utm_source=gbp p3.5 / p3.0. probe8: 'ryan realty' 3c/39i p40.0 (June) -> 0c/44i p40.7. probe11 homepage exact weekly p25 (07-06), p33 (07-27..08-10), p36 (08-17), p41 (08-24), p29 (09-07), p20 (09-14). findings.why_it_matters: Referrals, past clients and ad viewers who search the name do not land on the site. Brand search is also an entity signal for AI engines. Volume is small (tens of impressions/month), so this is minor.

Check the brand SERP for other 'Ryan Realty' firms (UNVERIFIED cause). Record a ledger row with the brand query position as the metric.

findings.title: site_signal GSC has permanent false zeros (2026-05-12..05-21) and an understated current week
findings.claim: The account series has zero-impression rows for 9 May days that GSC actually recorded, and the latest day is written as 0 until the 9-day rolling re-pull fixes it. Any 'this week vs peak' read from site_signal is understated (probe2 said -36%; the API says -28%).

findings.title: Tetherow blog (p15.7) was 301'd into the community page (p47.1) with no measurement
findings.claim: 136088a (09-22) redirects the page that ranks best for Tetherow queries into the page that ranks worst. A 301 usually passes most signals, but nothing records the before/after, so if the community page drops out of the SERP entirely the loop will not see it.
findings.evidence: probe15 08-31..09-20 tetherow queries: /blog/tetherow-resort-living-real-estate 154i p15.7; /communities/tetherow 136i p47.1. probe8: blog 3c/807i p9.6 in 08-23..09-19. Commit 136088a touches data/legacy-redirects.json and next.config.ts; no ledger row (probe7).
findings.why_it_matters: Tetherow is a p1 target community. Consolidation is the right direction (gsc-trend-4) only if the destination carries the blog's content and intent.
findings.proposed_fix: Write a ledger row now: metric = impression-weighted position and impressions for queries containing 'tetherow' on /communities/tetherow, baseline from probe15, window 28 days. Confirm the community page carries the blog's decision content. If position is not at or under ~p20 by the window end, revisit.

questions_for_matt: Do you or a vendor run a rank tracker that searches the quoted queries ("tetherow homes for sale", "broken top real estate", [brasada ranch real estate] ...)? Each shows about 3 impressions a day, every day, since May/June, with 0 clicks. Which tool is it? Its own export would be a cleaner position series than GSC.

S. Oregon listing pages brought 77 of 385 clicks (20%) in 08-24..09-13, and SITE-33 is removing them from the index. Confirm you want them out of search entirely, rather than indexed with a referral CTA.
Which page should own 'homes for sale {city}': /cities/{city} or /homes-for-sale/{city}? Today target_queries names /homes-for-sale/bend, which has zero impressions.
